content.title: About
content.content: Grade A eggs are whole large eggs of the highest quality, produced by chickens raised without hormones or antibiotics. The white and yolk are rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals, making them a versatile ingredient in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken eggs are one of the most widely consumed foods worldwide.
An egg contains all essential amino acids needed by humans.
A typical large egg weighs about 63–73 g.
Eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for 4–5 weeks without loss of quality.
The yolk contains lutein and zeaxanthin – antioxidants beneficial for eye health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: One large egg provides about 6 g of high‑quality protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and biotin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: The yolk is one of the few natural food sources of vitamin D, which aids bone health and immunity.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help protect eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Eggs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Egg allergy is common, especially in children; reactions can range from mild to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Salmonella risk
items.content: Raw or undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella bacteria; it is recommended to cook eggs thoroughly.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains cholesterol; individuals with high cholesterol should moderate yolk intake.

items.title: Storage contamination
items.content: Improper storage can lead to spoilage; keep eggs refrigerated and discard any with cracked shells.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eggs can be boiled, fried, scrambled, used in omelets, baked goods, sauces, and salads. For a milder flavor, the yolk can be separated and used separately.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store eggs in their original carton in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. Do not wash them before storage to preserve the natural protective coating. Use within 4–5 weeks, checking freshness with the float test.
